analysis.investment_thesis: GESHIP screens attractively on both Magic Formula metrics today — Earnings Yield ~14.6% (EBIT 2,677 / EV ~18,385 Cr) and ROIC ~20% (EBIT / invested capital of ~13,276 Cr) — but shipping is deeply cyclical and current earnings likely reflect a near-peak rate environment, making normalized metrics far less compelling. The fortress balance sheet (net cash ~1,949 Cr) and disciplined capital allocation are genuine strengths, but the 9-year EBITDA CAGR of only 1.7% reveals the structural earnings stagnation beneath cycle peaks.
key_strengths: Magic Formula Earnings Yield ~14.6% (EBIT 2,677 Cr / EV ~18,385 Cr) — well above the 12% attractiveness threshold
Near-net-cash balance sheet: debt collapsed from 5,295 Cr (2020) to 1,254 Cr (2025) while cash grew to 4,112 Cr — exceptional deleveraging
Strong FCF generation: 5/5 years positive OCF, FCF averaged ~2,200 Cr over last 3 years; Debt/Equity at 0.08
key_risks: Shipping is acutely cyclical — EBIT ranged from 1,067 Cr (2019) to 3,128 Cr (2023); normalized EY on 10-year avg EBIT (~1,892 Cr) drops to ~10.3%, below the compelling threshold
Rising capex (574→845→1,175 Cr) for fleet renewal will compress future FCF at a time when freight rates may be softening

9-year revenue CAGR of only 3.8% and EBITDA CAGR of 1.7% confirm this is not a growth compounder — Magic Formula works best with businesses sustaining high ROIC over time, which shipping historically cannot
red_flags: Net profit was negative in FY2018 (−210 Cr) and FY2019 (−21 Cr) — ROIC collapses in shipping downturns, violating the 3+ year ROIC sustainability requirement
Other income (834 Cr in FY25) is growing faster than operating income — inflating reported earnings quality
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on today's numbers: EV ≈ 20,334 + 2,163 − 4,112 = ~18,385 Cr; EBIT (FY25 operating income) = 2,677 Cr → Earnings Yield = 14.6%, very attractive. Invested capital = equity (15,225) + debt (2,163) − cash (4,112) = ~13,276 Cr → ROIC = ~20.2%, just crossing the "good" threshold. On the surface, this is a legitimate Magic Formula candidate — cheap AND decent returns on capital. The near-net-cash balance sheet and P/E of 9x with EV/EBITDA of 5.2x reinforce the value argument.

The critical flaw for a Greenblatt screen is that shipping earnings are notoriously mean-reverting. The 10-year average EBIT is ~1,892 Cr vs. the FY25 figure of 2,677 Cr — on normalized earnings, EY falls to ~10.3%, merely adequate. ROIC in prior cycle troughs was likely sub-12%, as evidenced by two years of negative net profit (FY18-19) and ROCE reported at just 13.9%. The Magic Formula demands businesses with durable competitive advantages that sustain high ROIC — commodity shipping lacks pricing power and moat. I'd want to see rates and earnings hold for another 1-2 years before treating current metrics as "real."
